blocks.text: Divide and Conquer (baanto aur jeeto) ek taqatwar algorithm design technique hai jo bare masle ko chhote aur manageable hisson mein torti hai. Har chhota hissa alag se hal hota hai, phir un ke hal jor kar asal masla hal kiya jata hai, jaisa Figure 3.6 mein dikhaya gaya hai. Yeh tareeqa khaas taur par un maslon ke liye faidemand hai jo milte julte chhote maslon mein toote ja sakte hain, kyun ke is se qadam ba qadam hal dhoondna aasan ho jata hai.

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Kitab ki figure mein [14, 7] ko baantne ke baad neeche 7 aur 14 ulti tarteeb mein chhape hain. Baantne (divide) se tarteeb nahi badalti, is liye yahan 14 aur 7 banaye gaye hain. Phir jorne (merge) ka step (qadam) aata hai jo figure mein alag nahi dikhaya gaya: [14] aur [7] mil kar [7, 14], [3] aur [12] mil kar [3, 12], aur aakhir mein dono mil kar [3, 7, 12, 14].

Misal: Merge Sort Divide and Conquer algorithm ki mashhoor misal hai. Algorithm be-tarteeb (unsorted) list ko do aadhon mein baant kar shuru karta hai. Phir har aadha alag se sort hota hai, aur aakhir mein dono sorted aadhe merge (jor) kar ke aakhri sorted list banti hai. Figure 3.6 Merge Sort ka process dikhati hai: list kaise baanti jati hai aur phir jor kar sorted output banta hai. Yeh tasveer dikhati hai ke Divide and Conquer tareeqa kitna efficient hai.
Yeh program Merge Sort ke divide (baantna) aur merge (jorna) ke qadam print karta hai, jaise Figure 3.6 mein. numbers list badal kar Run karein aur har qadam dekhein.

numbers = [14, 7, 3, 12]

def merge_sort(items, depth=0):
    print("  " * depth + "Divide:", items)
    if len(items) <= 1:
        return items
    mid = len(items) // 2
    left = merge_sort(items[:mid], depth + 1)       # sort each half
    right = merge_sort(items[mid:], depth + 1)
    merged = []
    i = j = 0
    while i < len(left) and j < len(right):         # merge: take the smaller front item
        if left[i] <= right[j]:
            merged.append(left[i])
            i += 1
        else:
            merged.append(right[j])
            j += 1
    merged = merged + left[i:] + right[j:]
    print("  " * depth + "Merge:", left, "+", right, "->", merged)
    return merged

print("Sorted:", merge_sort(numbers))

blocks.prompt: Kis algorithm ki time complexity O(n log n) hai: Bubble Sort, Binary Search, Merge Sort ya Insertion Sort (MCQ 10)?
blocks.explanation: (c) Merge Sort. Binary Search O(log n) hai; Bubble Sort aur Insertion Sort O(n²) hain.
